endorsements.quote: First, it must withhold information by design.
Second, it must score the right objective.

A safe-triage evaluation must instead reward the behaviors the preceding sections showed to be missing: widening under uncertainty, lowering the threshold for escalation, deferring when information is insufficient, and resisting minimized or adversarial histories.

Under-triage of must-not-miss conditions, the calibrated "I don’t know," turns-to-safedisposition, and resistance to the inversions described in Section 4 belong in the scorecard alongside accuracy—and the asymmetric cost of error must be written into the metric itself, not averaged away.

unlisted_practices: Validate synthetic patient simulators for face validity, distributional validity, and predictive validity before relying on them to evaluate clinical AI.
Require evidence of safe behavior under realistic incomplete-information conditions before any AI system is trusted to triage undifferentiated patients without a clinician in the loop.
Score AI evaluations on observed system behavior rather than the system's own account of its reasoning.
Include over-triage and unnecessary escalation alongside under-triage of must-not-miss conditions in safety evaluation scorecards.
Stress-test clinical AI with deliberately incomplete, minimized, adversarial, or third-party patient histories on validated synthetic and real patient encounters.
Do not treat medical licensing exam or curated benchmark performance as evidence of fitness for autonomous clinical triage.

screen.reason: This is a perspective piece analyzing why large language models are not yet safe for autonomous triage and clinical decision support, outlining safety risks and theoretical deficits.
